_idle_bringback_doc: DI1, CK4 in design/RimMandrake/operating_requirements_2026-11-01.md; seat_restart.py _bringback. A seat idle with ready work and nothing taken for idle_bringback_after_min is restarted once; its replacement has fresh_take_s to take work, else the alarm idle_bringback:<seat>, one incident in the told ledger. Unset or 0 turns it off. The limit, not no_handoff.escalate_after, starts the restart: the three rings of rering_s take 50 min, the target is 30.

busy_waiting._doc: BUSY_SEAT_FIX_WAITING_COUNTS_AS_WORK: `claude agents` keeps a window busy after its turn ended while a background helper or command lives (FOUNDRY 2026-11-01, about 4 h, 424 ready). dispatcher.busy_waiting reads such a window as idle turn_s past an ended turn, or tool_s inside one tool call with no helper alive and no question open; tool_s stands above the 600 s limit on a foreground command. Reads the main transcript; unreadable means busy. The restart fences keep the raw status: no window is killed on this reading.

_alarm_worse_doc: ALARM_REPEAT_FIX_BREAK_ON_WORSE: a repeat of an alarm kind inside alarm_every_s is raised anyway when its impact (the number the Dispatcher passes with it: helper age, ring streak, seconds dead) passes this kind's stated step past what was last told, factor or add; a kind with no row waits the 6 h. A severity carried on the action breaks it with no row.

no_handoff._doc: FOUNDRY_IDLE_REWIRE_PARKS_ON_LANE_WAITS (BENCH 2026-10-29): after a woke_no_handoff (doorbell consumed, no lease/claim/start in handoff_s) the seat is rung again after rering_s[k-1] s for its k-th consecutive one (the last entry bounds it), instead of the whole cooldown_s: that cooldown made ring FOUNDRY-1793297947-1 -> FOUNDRY-1793302231-1 4284 s apart (handoff_s 600 + cooldown_s 3600 + tick) while 798 items waited. Each ring is sent only when the seat's queue has work, so escalate_after consecutive ones raise an idle_full_queue:<SEAT> alarm (ledger note on escalate_item, null = alarm_item, rate-limited by alarm_every_s) and append a RAISE FIRST line to conductor_log (null = off). A hand-off or an empty queue ends the streak. Worst case: rings at ~0, ~16, ~43 min, then every ~40 min (handoff_s + 1800 + tick), escalated at ~53 min; under the 12/h cap.

long_helper._doc: CONDUCTOR_HELPERS_TUNE_TWENTY_MINUTE_WINDOW (owner 2026-10-29: "Long standing runs beyond n hour should raise an alarm in conductor."): a Conductor-window helper running longer than alarm_after_s raises a long_helper:<id> alarm (ledger note on item, null = alarm_item; RAISE FIRST line in no_handoff.conductor_log).

golive._doc: The set the owner's switch may turn on (design/RimMandrake/rimflow_v3_trial_night_2026-10-28.md). selftest_dispatcher.py refuses any role enabled but not named in roles, and any seat with recover_dead true but not named in recover_dead. A flip is one file: set the role's enabled true AND add its name here (likewise a seat's recover_dead and its name). The Dispatcher itself does not read this block.

_restart_reconcile_doc: CK3, read by Utils/restart_reconcile.py on its own timer, never by the Dispatcher. A request unmatched by restart_verified is told inside restart_reconcile_s: it alarms pass + slack earlier. held_s is the bound for a request waiting on helpers (journal: up to 64 min) until a cancel; a goodbye never gets it. hold_fresh_s is how long the last restart_hold line counts as the Dispatcher still holding: worst tick measured 237 s of 1869 (2026-10-30..11-01) + two 120 s passes. The pass unit's period must equal pass_s.

seat_restart._doc: seat_restart.dry true (with enabled true) runs the restart path under the live --apply timer without consuming, killing or launching: the live journal shows restart_request / restart_hold / restart_kill 'would SIGTERM' (the dry ticket in the enable steps). FOUNDRY_CONTEXT_BUILD_FRESH_PER_TICKET (owner 2026-10-28: "Yes we must solve foundry context right now."): a fresh window per ticket. The seat's close-out writes a restart request (seat_restart.py request); the Dispatcher holds it through a grace, while any helper is alive, while the bridge, driver lock or a game action is the seat's, and on any new input, then SIGTERMs that one pid; the tile relaunches itself (seat_loop.sh -> seat_restart.py intile) with the WT profile's own LAUNCH line (--remote-control, --name) plus a first prompt that runs `seat_restart.py wake`; verified once the doorbell re-arms. Every step journalled; failures alarm. Off until the enable steps in design/RimMandrake/rimflow_v3_golive_wave1.md (Seat restart) are done. Keys per seat override seat_restart.DEFAULTS.

BENCH._why_enabled: OWNER 2026-10-29: "Leave the goodbye kill on. If I'm typing at the same time it's an acceptable risk." (his ruling after blind review 3, D:\ClaudeWork\rimmandrake\v3_review\blind\goodbye\review3.md P0-1: check-then-kill on a live window cannot be made atomic). The goodbye restart is ON firing instantly, and no text can stop it (owner 2026-11-01). The context backstop is ON since 2026-11-01, see _why_backstop.
BENCH._why_hold: CONDUCTOR_RESET_FIX_KILLED_MID_READ, owner 2026-11-03: "I wish there were a switch I could click on Conductor that said \"hold for user interaction\" or \"ready to reset as soon as possible\" or \"auto\"". reset_mode.py. These two are hold's safety ceiling: past either, the ordinary limits apply again and he hears it once.
BENCH._why_backstop: Owner by card 2026-11-01: "Should the Conductor restart itself like Foundry? -> Same limits as Foundry". Every number here is FOUNDRY's, grace_s and quiet_s included (a goodbye ignores both: _goodbye; only goodbye_quiet_s 0 times it, and a goodbye during a pending backstop joins and fires at once: _join_request). backstop_human_idle_s stays 4 h on the SOFT line: Foundry has no such key, so nothing there says otherwise. It does NOT hold the HARD line: FOUNDRY's 200k fires whatever the window is doing, so on BENCH a 200k window restarts at its next ended turn plus 20 s of quiet even mid-conversation. His typing cancels, and the next tick re-arms. The told-once at the soft line never reaches BENCH, which has no doorbell. Review 3 F2/F3 closed in the same change (cursor at EOF of the read that found his last input).
BENCH._why: CONDUCTOR_GOODBYE_DESIGN_FRESH_EACH_TIME (design/RimMandrake/conductor_briefing_2026-10-28.md B2/B3): when his WHOLE message is one of goodbye_phrases (lower-cased, apostrophes dropped, other punctuation as spaces; .claude/hooks/conductor_goodbye.py), the Conductor window closes out (rulings --owner-said, promises --for OWNER, 3-5 lines to seat_log = no_handoff.conductor_log) and runs `seat_restart.py request --seat BENCH --fresh --reason goodbye`. kind conductor: the relaunch prompt is the Conductor's wake, not the doorbell ritual, and it is verified when the fresh window ends its first turn (BENCH has no doorbell). grace_s 120 is only the floor; goodbye_quiet_s 600 (blind review 2 P0-1, simplified 2026-10-29): the kill waits until the old transcript has been quiet for ten minutes on both clocks (newest record time after the goodbye cursor, and the Dispatcher's own last-seen-growth time) with every record parsed cleanly (the owner's machine idle clock is not read: owner 2026-10-30, strip "when I come back to the machine" as an event for anything changing). ANY input after the goodbye cancels (his, a ring, a task notification, a queue enqueue); a malformed record cancels; a half-written record holds. The relaunch prompt passes the restart's --gen, so the wake replays exactly that restart's messages once.
